reason: Both conversations over-committed to 'almost certainly the battery' and neither suggested Dyson support diagnosis or a known-good battery swap before spending money, but Conversation 2 at least hedged once ('can't be 100% certain without testing'), stayed consistent with the facts the customer gave, and sensibly used Normal-mode runtime as a cheap discriminator. Conversation 1 opened by pushing the already-ruled-out blockage/overheating theory, then, after correctly asking for the label, misidentified SV11 as a V8 (it's a V7) - a factual error that could lead to buying the wrong battery pack, which undermines its one real advantage of having asked for the model. Conversation 1 did include a switch-off safety line and the charger-contact check, so the gap is narrow.
